title: VOCE Agent Infrastructure Reference — Europe 2026
status: VOCE public reference architecture; not an EU or ISO standard
purpose: A vendor-neutral control and interoperability reference for institutions deploying AI agents, APIs, tool protocols and multi-agent systems in Europe.

design_principles.name: Identity before action
design_principles.rule: Every executing agent or workload must have an attributable identity distinct from the human, service or model that initiated it.

design_principles.name: Least authority
design_principles.rule: Permissions, data scopes, tools and transaction limits are granted per task and are revocable.

design_principles.name: Contracted interfaces
design_principles.rule: APIs, tools and inter-agent messages use explicit machine-readable contracts, versioning and validation.

design_principles.name: Traceable delegation
design_principles.rule: Delegation chains record who delegated what authority to which agent, for which purpose, duration and resources.

design_principles.name: Observable execution
design_principles.rule: Model calls, retrieval, tool calls, agent handoffs, approvals, failures, cost and final actions can be reconstructed.

design_principles.name: Human authority
design_principles.rule: Material decisions define an accountable human owner, escalation path and executable stop mechanism.

design_principles.name: Reversibility
design_principles.rule: Models, tools and vendors can be restricted, replaced or revoked without disabling the wider institutional system.

design_principles.name: Regulatory mapping
design_principles.rule: EU legal obligations are mapped to the actual role, sector and risk classification of the deployed system rather than applied generically.

layers.name: API and tool contracts
layers.objective: Make every callable capability explicit, typed, versioned and testable.

layers.name: Model-to-tool and context interoperability
layers.objective: Expose tools, resources and context through a governed interface rather than bespoke prompt wiring.
layers.note: MCP 2026-07-28 uses a stateless protocol core and includes authorization hardening; protocol interoperability does not replace institutional authorization policy.

layers.name: Agent-to-agent interoperability
layers.objective: Allow independent agents to discover capabilities, exchange tasks and collaborate across vendor or framework boundaries.
layers.note: A2A defines interoperability; trust, authorization and accountability still belong to the deploying institution.

layers.name: Workload and agent identity
layers.objective: Give software actors cryptographically verifiable, short-lived identities independent of network location.

layers.name: Authorization and delegation
layers.objective: Decide whether a principal may perform a specific action on a specific resource in context.

layers.name: Data, memory and RAG lifecycle
layers.objective: Keep institutional knowledge, access rights and deletion state aligned from source system through retrieval and memory.

layers.name: Observability and audit
layers.objective: Reconstruct an agentic execution end-to-end without relying on narrative reconstruction.

layers.name: Evaluation, security and continuous assurance
layers.objective: Test the deployed system as a changing socio-technical system, not only the foundation model.

layers.name: Economic authority and FinOps
layers.objective: Treat spending capacity as an operational permission.

layers.name: European regulatory overlay
layers.objective: Map technical controls to the institution's actual EU role, sector and risk classification.
mandatory_controls: Third-party ICT register for DORA entities
Incident and cyber obligations by sector
layers.note: Applicability is contextual. The reference does not classify every agent as high-risk or subject every institution to DORA/NIS2.

maturity_levels.name: Assistant
maturity_levels.description: Generates or retrieves content; no external action authority.

maturity_levels.name: Tool-connected agent
maturity_levels.description: Can call approved read or low-impact tools.

maturity_levels.name: Delegated action agent
maturity_levels.description: Can execute business actions under bounded delegated authority.

maturity_levels.name: Multi-agent operating system
maturity_levels.description: Multiple agents coordinate tasks, models and tools across systems.

maturity_levels.name: Critical agent network
maturity_levels.description: Agentic execution can materially affect regulated, financial, clinical, infrastructure or public-service outcomes.

board_evidence_pack: Kill-switch, rollback and exit test evidence
